name: Stéphanie Yon-Courtin-Accord provisoire-Am 2
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014 as regards the modernisation of the key information document
part_text: AMENDMENTS BY THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT\* to the Commission proposal REGULATION (EU) 2026/… OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of … amending Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014 as regards the modernisation of the key information document (Text with EEA relevance) THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND THE COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION, Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and in particular Article 114 thereof, Having regard to the proposal from the European Commission, After transmission of the draft legislative act to the national parliaments, Having regard to the opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee, Acting in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure, Whereas: (1) A core objective of the Capital Markets Union is to ensure that consumers can fully benefit from the investment opportunities offered by capital markets. To be able to do so, consumers need to be supported by a regulatory framework that empowers them to take investment decisions that correspond to their needs and aims, and that adequately protects them in the internal market. The package of measures under the Union’s retail investment strategy seeks to address the identified shortcomings, including as regards the information to be made available to retail investors. (2) Article 4, point (1), of Regulation(EU) No 1286/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council defines packaged retail investment products (PRIPs) as investments where, regardless of the legal form of the investment, the amount repayable to the retail investor is subject to fluctuations because of exposure to reference values or to the performance of one or more assets which are not directly purchased by the retail investor. However, the possibility of the manufacturer redeeming the investment early by activating a make-whole clause should not in itself be considered to be such a fluctuation. That clarification should be reflected in the definition of PRIPs. (3) Where packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) offer the retail investor a range of investment options, information on those options might be contained in different documents. That makes it difficult for retail investors interested in purchasing such PRIIPs to identify their total cost.
